speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific location of your wrist pain, when the fever started, and what the skin lesions look like. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; CRP: NOT PROVIDED; ESR: NOT PROVIDED. Additional findings from prior data include Joint Aspiration of left wrist showing >50,000 WBC/μL and Gram-negative diplococci, and STI screening positive for Gonorrhea.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia seems unrelated to your acute wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; could you please describe exactly what those skin lesions look like and whether the pain feels throbbing or constant? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Iron studies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC WITH DIFFERENTIAL: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; IRON STUDIES: NOT PROVIDED. Additional findings from prior data include Joint Aspiration of left wrist showing >50,000 WBC/μL and Gram-negative diplococci, and STI screening positive for Gonorrhea. Skin lesions are described as painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The clinical picture of fever, migratory wrist pain with negative trauma history, and pathognomonic painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the extremities, combined with positive gonorrhea screening and Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate, confirms this diagnosis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology images of wrist lesions.
